environment.zfs: available: OpenZFS 2.1.11-1+deb12u1 built by DKMS for 6.1.0-54-amd64; zfs-whole passes the raw /dev/vdb block device straight to zpool with no partition, loop device, or file-backed vdev; zfs (legacy) keeps its separately labelled file-backed vdev

method.cold: guest runs `sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` immediately before the run
method.warm: the next run on the same files, with no cache drop
method.zfs_whole_disk: zfs-whole passes /dev/vdb directly to `zpool create -f -m /data/tank tank /dev/vdb`; no partition, loop device, or file-backed vdev is used for that target
method.zfs_legacy_file_vdev: the separate zfs target remains the earlier file-backed vdev and is not a whole-disk result
method.btrfs: mkfs.btrfs on the host, guest insmods btrfs.ko and mounts /dev/vdb
method.results_disk: raw ext4 virtio-blk, extracted with debugfs; no loop mount
method.root: read-only ext4 image built in the vm court
method.vms: QEMU -smp 4 -m 1536M; the host court is limited to 4 CPUs and 3 GiB
method.weftfs: Rust and Go WeftFS are mounted over FUSE inside the guest; store and mount live on the ext4 data disk
method.zero_buffers: fio write buffers default to zeros; WeftFS chunk dedup can therefore reduce stored bytes. This receipt measures latency/IOPS, not storage amplification.
method.not_claimed: No physical power loss, no host page-cache drop, no device write-cache loss. ZFS reads are ARC-served unless the pool cache is separately emptied; drop_caches does not drop the ZFS ARC.
